meta.rule:
One record per body, combining every source that names it:
  - the territory's constitution or founding Order in Council on legislation.gov.uk (the establishing clause is quoted and
    must be found in sources/evidence/territory-instruments.json, which carries each order's fingerprint);
  - the body's own or its government's official website, where the page was read and named the body;
  - Wikidata (community-sourced, CC0): legislature, executive and court links, other public bodies, and official websites.
Nothing is inferred from a name alone: a constitutional body needs its clause; any other body needs a Wikidata record whose
class is a public-sector class. Bodies whose website no longer answers are kept and flagged, not dropped.
Writes data/territories.json. --negative proves the checks fail when they should.

GI.name: Gibraltar
GI.note: Gibraltar's Constitution Order 2006 is not published on legislation.gov.uk, so its bodies here rest on Wikidata and official websites.

GS.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

IO.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
IO.note: A treaty signed in May 2025 would transfer sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius, with the UK keeping the base on Diego Garcia. It is not in force: the UK's enabling legislation ran out of time in Parliament in 2026. Until it is, this remains a UK Overseas Territory.

note_sources.title: GOV.UK: UK/Mauritius Agreement concerning the Chagos Archipelago including Diego Garcia (May 2025)
Chatham House, January 2026: Lords debate on ratification delayed

meta.blocked: The Isle of Man Government's website refused automated checks, so its departments known only from Wikidata are left out until they can be confirmed another way; the site was not retried with a disguised request.
meta.not_covered: Local government below the jurisdiction (parishes, parish commissioners, douzaines) is shown only where the body's own website confirms it; hospitals are left out because the sources don't say whether each is public or private.
